raw_tool_response: User responded: reporting_boundaries=Q7-C01 — REPORTING ANCHOR AND EXACT BOUNDARIES  1. REPORTING ANCHOR  The first release must use an explicitly recorded, selectable synthetic scenario reporting anchor timestamp.  Reports must not silently depend on the current live system clock for historical or synthetic reporting calculations.  The reporting anchor must be preserved with each generated report so that the same synthetic dataset, anchor, filters, and calculation definitions produce reproducible results.  The anchor must include an identifiable UTC timestamp and its corresponding Asia/Kolkata display value.  Changing the reporting anchor must be an explicit user action.  2. LAST 7/30/90 DAYS CALCULATION  Last 7, Last 30, and Last 90 Days must represent calendar-day periods in Asia/Kolkata (IST), not rolling 24-hour intervals.  The anchor's local calendar date is included in the reporting period.  For an anchor date D:  - Last 7 Days: D-6 through D, inclusive. - Last 30 Days: D-29 through D, inclusive. - Last 90 Days: D-89 through D, inclusive.  The reporting period starts at 00:00 IST on the calculated start date and ends at 00:00 IST on the calendar day following the anchor date.  This produces an inclusive start boundary and exclusive end boundary.  3. START AND END BOUNDARY RULES  All reporting queries must follow the same interval convention:  StartTimestampUtc <= EventTimestampUtc < EndTimestampUtc  The start boundary is inclusive.  The end boundary is exclusive.  An event occurring exactly at the start boundary is included.  An event occurring exactly at the end boundary is excluded.  This avoids duplicate counting when adjacent reporting periods are compared.  4. CUSTOM DATE-RANGE CONVERSION  Custom date ranges must be selected and interpreted as Asia/Kolkata calendar dates.  Both the selected start date and selected end date are inclusive from the user's perspective.  For calculation purposes:  - Start boundary: 00:00 IST on the selected start date. - End boundary: 00:00 IST on the calendar day immediately following the selected end date.  Both boundaries must then be converted to UTC before querying stored event timestamps.  The system must validate that the start date is not later than the end date.  The report must retain the original selected local dates, timezone, and converted UTC boundaries.  5. PENDING-STATE COUNTS  Pending request counts must represent the request lifecycle state as of the selected reporting anchor timestamp.  Only valid lifecycle events recorded at or before the reporting anchor may determine the state at that anchor.  Requests created after the anchor must not be included.  Requests resolved or otherwise transitioned after the anchor must retain their earlier state when reconstructing the anchor-time snapshot.  Pending-state counts are point-in-time snapshot metrics, not counts of events occurring during the reporting period.  The first release will use the synthetic scenario anchor for these calculations.  Actual live application snapshots, if introduced in a future release, must be separately labelled and must not be mixed with synthetic historical snapshots.  6. REPRODUCIBILITY AND REPORT EVIDENCE  Every generated report must preserve:  - Reporting anchor timestamp. - Reporting timezone. - Selected reporting period. - Original custom date-range selections, if applicable. - UTC start and end boundaries. - Applied filters. - Metric-definition version. - Synthetic dataset/scenario identifier. - Calculation and data-quality context.  Generating the same report using the same dataset, anchor, filters, and metric-definition version must produce the same results.  7. FINAL DECISION  The first release will use a selectable, recorded synthetic scenario anchor rather than the live clock for reproducible synthetic reporting.  Last 7/30/90 Days will use IST calendar days, including the anchor day, with an inclusive start boundary and exclusive end boundary.  Custom date ranges will use inclusive local calendar dates and be converted into UTC boundaries before querying.  Pending-state metrics will represent the lifecycle state at the selected reporting anchor.  Live application snapshots remain a separate, explicitly labelled future capability.  These decisions clarify reporting calculation boundaries only. They do not introduce an SLA, authorize ticket changes, approve the PRD, or authorize implementation., review_denominators=Q7-C02 — COMPLETED REVIEW POPULATION AND COUNTING UNIT  1. COUNTING UNIT  The primary counting unit will be one completed, eligible human review decision per classification field per review cycle.  Category, Priority, and Queue must be measured independently.  A single ticket containing three classification fields may therefore contribute up to three completed review decisions.  Ticket count and classification-field decision count must not be treated as interchangeable metrics.  2. COMPLETED REVIEW OUTCOMES  Every completed eligible review decision must have one distinct final outcome:  A. ACCEPTED The human reviewer accepts the AI-suggested value without changing it.  B. REJECTED The human reviewer rejects the AI suggestion without accepting it as the final classification.  C. OVERRIDDEN The human reviewer replaces the AI-suggested value with a different human-selected value.  Accepted, Rejected, and Overridden outcomes must remain mutually exclusive and separately identifiable.  3. DENOMINATOR FOR ACCEPTANCE AND OVERRIDE RATES  All completed eligible review decisions must be included in the denominator, including rejected suggestions.  The denominator is:  Accepted + Rejected + Overridden  Acceptance Rate:  Accepted / (Accepted + Rejected + Overridden) × 100  Override Rate:  Overridden / (Accepted + Rejected + Overridden) × 100  Rejection Rate:  Rejected / (Accepted + Rejected + Overridden) × 100  Rejected suggestions must not be silently excluded from the denominator.  All three outcomes must reconcile to the total completed eligible review population.  4. FIELD-LEVEL REPORTING  Category, Priority, and Queue metrics must be calculated and reported separately.  The dashboard may additionally provide an overall combined classification decision summary, provided the underlying field-level populations remain independently identifiable.  Reports must not mix different classification fields in a way that hides their individual acceptance, rejection, or override behaviour.  5. REPEATED DECISIONS AND REVIEW CYCLES  Multiple edits or decision changes within the same review cycle must not inflate completed review counts.  Only the final completed eligible decision for each classification field within that review cycle will contribute to the primary outcome metrics.  All intermediate decisions and changes must remain available in the authorized audit history.  A separately initiated and authorized new review cycle may count as a new review decision.  Each decision must retain its record reference, field, review-cycle identifier, original AI suggestion, final human-confirmed value, outcome, reviewer identity, and relevant timestamps.  6. EXCLUDED POPULATIONS  The following must not be included in completed eligible review denominators:  - Pending reviews. - Unassessed classifications. - Ineligible records. - Incomplete review decisions. - Processing-only records without a completed human decision. - Rejected or expired lifecycle records that are not eligible for review.  A rejected AI suggestion is different from a rejected document or knowledge lifecycle record. These concepts must not be confused.  7. ZERO DENOMINATOR AND DATA QUALITY  When the completed eligible review denominator is zero, the applicable acceptance, rejection, and override rates must display N/A rather than zero percent.  Missing, invalid, or conflicting review evidence must be identified rather than silently included or excluded.  All metrics must preserve tenant isolation and the applicable reporting-anchor boundaries established in Q7-C01.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release will use completed eligible human review decisions per classification field per review cycle as its primary counting unit.  Accepted, Rejected, and Overridden outcomes will be distinct.  All three outcomes, including completed rejected suggestions, will be included in the acceptance, rejection, and override rate denominators.  Repeated changes within the same review cycle will not inflate the primary decision counts. Historical changes will remain auditable.  Pending, Unassessed, Ineligible, and incomplete decisions will be excluded.  A zero denominator will produce N/A.  These decisions clarify analytics counting rules only. They do not change Q1-Q6 authorization, lifecycle, retention, tenant-isolation, or security requirements, and do not authorize implementation., rationale_deferrals=Q7-C03 — RATIONALE AND REMAINING CALCULATION DEFERRALS  1. RATIONALE FOR REPORTING ANCHOR AND DATE BOUNDARIES  A selectable, recorded synthetic reporting anchor is preferred over the live system clock because it provides reproducible and verifiable reporting results.  Using Asia/Kolkata calendar days provides consistent reporting periods for the first release.  An inclusive start boundary and exclusive end boundary prevent duplicate counting when adjacent reporting periods are compared.  Converting local reporting boundaries into UTC ensures consistency with the underlying UTC event storage.  Preserving the reporting anchor, selected dates, filters, scenario identifier, and metric-definition version makes historical synthetic reports reproducible.  2. RATIONALE FOR COMPLETED REVIEW COUNTING  Counting completed eligible human decisions independently for Category, Priority, and Queue provides meaningful field-level classification analytics.  Keeping Accepted, Rejected, and Overridden outcomes separate prevents misleading acceptance and override calculations.  Including completed rejected suggestions in the denominator ensures that acceptance rates reflect the entire completed eligible review population.  Counting only the final decision within a review cycle prevents intermediate edits from artificially inflating performance metrics.  Retaining the complete review history preserves auditability without confusing historical changes with completed review counts.  3. REMAINING CALCULATION DEFERRALS  The following calculation definitions and capabilities remain explicitly deferred:  A. BUSINESS CALENDAR AND SLA CALCULATIONS - Business-hours calculations. - Working-day and holiday exclusions. - Priority-specific SLA targets. - SLA breach thresholds. - SLA compliance calculations. - SLA pause and resume rules.  B. ADVANCED REQUEST LIFECYCLE ANALYTICS - Cumulative resolution time across multiple reopen cycles. - Advanced repeated-resolution calculations. - Reopened-request SLA calculations. - Advanced historical lifecycle performance comparisons.  C. ADVANCED CLASSIFICATION ANALYTICS - Cross-reviewer performance ranking. - Advanced reviewer productivity and efficiency scoring. - Statistical confidence thresholds for classification performance. - Advanced multi-cycle reviewer comparison.  D. ADDITIONAL DATA AND RETENTION POLICIES - Actual customer-data analytics. - Advanced analytics dataset retention. - Content-bearing interaction history retention. - Additional aggregation and anonymization rules.  These capabilities must remain unavailable or explicitly gated until their definitions, authorization, data requirements, and calculation rules are separately approved.  4. DATA QUALITY AND UNDEFINED CALCULATIONS  All reporting calculations must use valid, traceable source events and the previously established reporting boundaries.  Missing, invalid, conflicting, or insufficient data must be identified explicitly.  A zero denominator must produce N/A rather than zero percent.  The system must not invent missing timestamps, assume unavailable values, silently substitute defaults, or present unverified calculations as established results.  Synthetic and actual application events must remain distinguishable.  5. FIRST-RELEASE SCOPE AND SAFEGUARDS  The first release will focus on reproducible synthetic analytics, reporting, classification decision metrics, and operational visibility.  The previously established tenant isolation, role permissions, human approval requirements, knowledge lifecycle, deletion, retention, and audit controls remain unchanged.  Dashboard recommendations remain informational.  No automatic ticket modifications, escalation, outgoing messages, external integrations, or production SLA commitments are introduced.  6. FINAL DECISION  The Q7-C01 reporting anchor and boundary rules and Q7-C02 completed review counting rules are accepted as the first-release calculation baseline.  Only explicitly defined and validated calculations may be displayed.  Undefined calculations, numeric targets, advanced analytics, business calendars, and operational policies remain deferred rather than being populated with assumed defaults.  This preserves reporting consistency, auditability, and the intended synthetic/local-only first-release boundary.  These decisions clarify calculation requirements only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, or permission to start another process.
